inputs.text: Micheál Martin was in Limerick this past week trying to spin that housing tenancies have gone up, but the real damage comes from the government's March 1 rules forcing landlords to offer six-year leases. Those heavy-handed mandates have triggered a clear rise in eviction notices and homelessness, and nationally the number of people in emergency accommodation has increased again. This is what happens when politicians override private agreements and property rights with top-down controls that drive landlords out of the market entirely. It undermines family stability and social order by reducing available homes instead of letting responsible owners and tenants work things out. These progressive interventions never deliver and only make the housing mess worse for ordinary people who value self-reliance over endless government fixes.
